Let an∈ℕ and A=∑n≥0an2−n−1<∞. For every cutoff K and every f:ℕ→ℝ tending to infinity, there are a set S⊆[K,∞) of upper Banach density zero and a nondegenerate interval I⊂(A,∞) with the following property. Every r∈I has the form

r=∑n≥0(an+en)2−n−1,

where en∈ℕ is supported on S, en≤f(n) eventually, and, for every integer q≥1, there is an Nq, chosen independently of r, such that

q∣enandq∣∑i<nei(n≥Nq).

For every ε>0, the construction can instead be chosen with en≤(log⁡(n+3))ε eventually and |S∩[X,2X)|=Oε(X/log⁡log⁡X). In that case the empirical distributions of original and corrected unnormalised blocks of length m(X)=o(log⁡log⁡X), sampled at the same integer starts in [X,2X), have total variation distance tending to zero, uniformly over r. Precisely the coupling error is at most m|S∩[X,2X+m)|/X; with ‖Φ‖∞≤B0 the bounded-test error is at most twice this quantity times B0, also for tests depending on the starting index.
